title: Finding
description: One evidence-backed problem detected by an analysis skill. Every analysis skill in this marketplace emits candidates in exactly this shape; the orchestrator merges them and assigns the final sequential id.

id.description: Sequential id assigned by the orchestrator after sorting. Analysis skills may emit a placeholder; it is always overwritten.

check_id.description: Stable registry id. Must exist in the owning skill's references/checks.yaml. Never renumber a check id once published; retire it instead.

title.description: One line naming the problem in the site owner's language, not ours. State the defect, not the check.

confidence.description: high: the evidence is dispositive. medium: strongly indicated, a benign explanation exists. low: suspected, needs human confirmation.

determinism.description: deterministic: derived from a bundled script over the evidence bundle; re-running yields the identical result. model-judged: reached by agent judgment. A model-judged finding may not be critical without deterministic corroboration.

category.description: Which half of the Round-2 problem this belongs to.

mechanism.description: Which stage of the pipeline fails. Ordered: a failure at an earlier stage makes later stages moot.

evidence.description: Quantified and human-readable, citing what was observed on how many pages. 'Crawled 12 product pages; 0/12 contain schema.org markup.' Never a restatement of the title.

pages_affected.description: URLs or bundle page-ids exhibiting the problem. Must be EXHAUSTIVE within the sampled set, never a sample of a sample -- the orchestrator derives scope from this list's length, so a truncated list gets the finding demoted under false-positive gate 5. The sample is capped at 25 pages, so an exhaustive list is always short.

artifact_refs.description: Bundle-relative paths backing this finding, e.g. 'pages/p003/extracted.json' or 'robots.txt.raw'. A finding whose refs are empty or unresolvable is dropped by the orchestrator, not downgraded.

excerpt.description: Verbatim snippet from the artifact, when a quote makes the finding self-evident.

scope.description: site-wide requires >=3 pages checked and >=60% affected.

section.description: Path prefix when scope is 'section', e.g. '/blog/'.

verification.description: One concrete step letting a human re-check this without our tooling. 'curl -A ChatGPT-User https://site/robots.txt and look for the Disallow.' This is what makes the report trustworthy rather than oracular.

severity_locked.description: When true the orchestrator applies no scope or confidence modifier to this finding. Set only by checks whose registry entry fixes the level -- informational findings such as a deliberate training-crawler opt-out, where escalation would contradict a binding false-positive guard.

superseded_by.description: check_ids of earlier-stage root causes that explain this finding. Set by the orchestrator during cross-mechanism merge.

summary.description: The fix in one imperative line. 'Add Product/Offer JSON-LD to every product page.'

steps.description: Ordered, concrete steps. Name the file, directive, tag or template to change. Never 'improve your structured data'.

code.description: Copy-pasteable snippet — JSON-LD block, robots.txt stanza, meta tag. Must be tailored to this site using values observed in the bundle, not a generic template with placeholders.

effort.description: S: a config or template edit, under an hour. M: a scoped content or code change, days. L: structural, weeks.

impact_rationale.description: Why this fix resolves the mechanism that is failing. Must reference the mechanism, not restate the fix. This is the field that proves the recommendation is mechanism-sound rather than cargo-culted.

owner.description: Who typically executes this, to help route the backlog.
